title: RFID Door
intro: Tap the right card to open the door. The wrong card gets a red light.

steps.title: Read a card
steps.text:
RFID cards have a tiny chip and an aerial inside. The reader powers the chip with radio waves, and the chip answers with its ID.

**Your task:** Run, open the **Serial Monitor**, and hold a card or tag on the reader. Write down its ID: you'll need it!
hints: Hold the card flat, right on the reader, for a second.
In the simulator, click the card next to the reader.
Each card has its own ID.

checks.label: I wrote down my card's ID

steps.success: Your reader works. Every card has its own ID, like a name tag.

steps.title: Open for the right card
steps.text:
Now the door: the right card turns the green light on and opens the latch for 3 seconds. Any other card gets the red light.

**Your task:** put your card's ID in `ALLOWED`, and fill in the blank.
hints: Compare the card's ID with the allowed one.
The allowed ID is in the constant `ALLOWED`.

checks.label: My card opens the door; another doesn't

steps.success: A card-operated door! Only your card works.

steps.title: Many cards and a log
steps.text: **Goal:** allow a **list** of 3 cards (use an array), and keep a log: every tap prints a visit number, the card's ID, and `Welcome!` or `Access denied`.
hints: Use a `for` loop to check the card against each one in the list.
Count visits in a variable and print it first.

checks.label: The allowed cards are a list

steps.success: A door with an access list and a log: just like a real building's security system.

outro: Your door reads cards with **RFID**, checks them against a **list** of allowed cards, and keeps a log. That's how school, office and transport cards work.
stretch: Add a "master card" that adds new cards to the allowed list.
Show the time each card was used (seconds since start) in the log.
Make a buzzer give a short beep for yes and a long one for no.
